references.text: Peter quotes directly from Deuteronomy 18:15 and applies this prophetic promise to Jesus as the prophet Moses predicted would come, emphasizing that the people must listen to him.
Stephen quotes this verse in his speech and identifies Jesus as the fulfillment of Moses' prophecy about a coming prophet like himself.
The people ask John the Baptist if he is 'the Prophet,' a reference to the expectation of the prophet Moses predicted in Deuteronomy 18:15.
Philip tells Nathanael that they have found the one Moses wrote about in the Law, a clear reference to the prophecy in Deuteronomy 18:15.
After the bread miracle, the people declare that Jesus is 'the Prophet who is to come into the world,' a direct connection to the expectation from Deuteronomy 18:15.
Some in the crowd identify Jesus as 'the Prophet,' based on the expectation of the prophet Moses predicted.
God confirms the promise to raise up a prophet and warns of the consequences for those who do not listen to his words.
The text confirms that no prophet like Moses had arisen in Israel, pointing forward to the fulfillment of the promise in Deuteronomy 18:15.
